records.source: Two kinds of thing are installed from a click: a segmentation backend, which is a Python package added to the running environment with ``pip`` (DINOCell and SAMCell, :data:`spacr.model_zoo.INSTALLABLE_BACKENDS`), and a Cellpose checkpoint from the model zoo, which is a file downloaded and verified by :func:`spacr.model_zoo.install`. records.label: spacr.qt.night_themes#3
records.source: THE PALETTES ARE LITERALS RATHER THAN A RECIPE. Keeping the numbers here rather than the recipe means the published colours are the reviewed colours, no solver runs at import, and ``tests/qt/test_ten_night_themes.py`` judges what actually ships.

records.translation: AS PALETAS SÃO LITERAIS, E NÃO UMA RECEITA. records.label: spacr.qt.night_themes#4
records.source: THREE COLOURS WERE MOVED OFF THE RECIPE BY MEASUREMENT, and they are the only three. records.label: spacr.qt.preferences.resolve_effective_theme#1
records.source: Resolves an explicitly chosen ``"system"`` to the operating system's colour scheme as Qt reports it (``QStyleHints.colorScheme``), and to dark when Qt can't tell. It does not read the application palette: that is spaCR's own once a theme has been applied, so it would answer with whatever was applied last. Every other value passes through, so callers that only understand light/dark should compare against ``"light"`` and treat everything else as dark (Space and Cell are dark themes).

records.translation: Resolve um ``"system"`` escolhido explicitamente para o esquema de cores do sistema operacional tal como o Qt o informa (``QStyleHints.colorScheme``), e para o escuro quando o Qt não consegue dizer. Todos os outros valores passam sem alteração, então chamadores que só entendem claro/escuro devem comparar com ``"light"`` e tratar todo o resto como escuro (Space e Cell são temas escuros).
